clue.text: They're stony, but may well get credit in interviews

indicators.note: the word in tells us the credit abbreviation is placed inside the word for interviews

parts.note: to see someone can mean to interview them, as a doctor or manager sees people
CR is the standard accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Stony things that might nonetheless earn credit when discussed in job interviews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may well get' is padding that links the definition to the wordplay; 'interviews' is a verb in the surface but stands for seeing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Screes are slopes of loose broken rock, so they are stony things.

clue.text: Ask for one of the little people-—fifty stone!

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous sprite, one of the fairy folk
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
ore is rock or stone from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a tiny fairy figure, exclaiming at its weight of fifty stone.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to beg or plead, a stronger way of asking for something.

clue.text: The fighter read a number before backing up 19

parts.note: to con a text is an old verb meaning to study or read it
ten is a number

indicators.note: in a down clue backing up means the referenced word runs upwards, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: the answer to 19 across is the colour red

explanation.surface: A boxer studies a figure before supporting the clue numbered nineteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is a competitor, such as a boxer fighting for a title.

clue.text: Form of decoration conferred on the French petty officer

parts.note: a bead is a small ornament, a form of decoration
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A decoration in some form is awarded to the French minor official.
explanation.walkthrough: A beadle is a minor parish or church official, which is the sense of petty officer here, not a naval rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle was a minor parish official, a petty officer who kept order in church.

clue.text: Quietly tease odd characters into giving a little cash

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for playing quietly

indicators.note: the letters of tease are made into odd, unusual characters, that is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone softly teases strange people into handing over a small sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters' tempts a solver to take alternate letters, but here it means the word is shuffled into strange shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was the Spanish unit of currency, a small amount of money.

clue.text: Sweet pie stall newly set up

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are set up afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A confectionery stall selling pies has just been erected at a market.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small sweet, often a chewy fruit-flavoured lozenge.

clue.text: Run out and make light of it

definitions.meaning: liquid that runs out of a container ... over
a thin twist of paper or wood used to carry a flame to a candle or pipe

explanation.definitionFit: To spill is to let liquid escape, and a spill is a taper used for lighting a fire.

clue.text: Get rat in proper shape by giving medical attention

indicators.note: the letters are knocked into a new shape, which signals a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone gets their car into good condition by tending it like a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: The page as held reads 'car', which cannot give two Ts; the wordplay needs GETRATIN rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating a patient means giving them medical care.

clue.text: Undisturbed, so was able to produce original work

definitions.text: was able to produce original work
definitions.meaning: wrote music or verse of one's own creation

explanation.definitionFit: Composed means calm, and a composer writes original music.

clue.text: Mass held in a ship or court

indicators.note: held in means the word for mass sits inside the abbreviation for ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
size or bulk is a sense of mass

explanation.surface: A church service is held aboard a vessel or in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks religious but means bulk, SIZE; 'or' is a link. The Assizes were periodic English county courts.
explanation.definitionFit: The assizes were periodic sessions of the higher courts held in English counties.

clue.text: We hear tail-back includes a hundred for show

indicators.note: includes means the reversed word holds the hundred inside it
back tells us the story word is turned round and read the other way
we hear signals that a word sounding like tail is wanted, spelt differently

parts.note: a tale is a story, and sounds the same as tail
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A traffic jam supposedly contains a hundred cars, laid on for display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail-back' suggests a traffic queue; instead TALE (sounding like 'tail') is turned to ELAT by 'back', and 'includes' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant display or conspicuous success, a flourish made for show.

clue.text: Support is delayed but put into force

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
late means delayed or behind time

explanation.surface: Backing for a measure is held up but it is finally enacted.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, putting rules into legal force.

clue.text: Cattle-fodder should include this plant

indicators.note: include means the plant's letters are contained within the clue's words

explanation.surface: Feed for cows ought to contain this particular plant.
explanation.walkthrough: ERS is bitter vetch, a plant once grown as fodder, so the surface is literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: Ers is an old name for bitter vetch, a leguminous plant.

clue.text: The foreigner a good man phoned with evident hesitation

parts.note: ST abbreviates saint, a good man
rang means telephoned
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: The overseas visitor telephoned a virtuous man, hesitating noticeably.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranger is an outsider, someone from elsewhere, as a foreigner is.

clue.text: The complaint could be mental

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: The patient's illness might be a psychological one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' suggests an illness; here it is an expression of grief.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament is a mournful expression of sorrow or grievance.

clue.text: Allowing a girl to enter a seedy bar

indicators.note: to enter means the girl goes into the word for a seedy bar

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar or club, and the article gives its own letter
miss is a young woman or girl

explanation.surface: A man permits a young woman to go into a sleazy drinking den.
explanation.definitionFit: Admissive is a rare word for permitting or letting in.

clue.text: A bed-sit in the West Country for the sponger?

parts.note: Bath is a city in the West Country, south-west England
a bed-sit is a single rented room

explanation.surface: A one-room flat in south-west England is offered to a freeloader.
explanation.walkthrough: A sponger is usually a scrounger; here it is someone washing with a sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathroom is the place where one washes with a sponge.

clue.text: Object within fourteen days

indicators.note: within shows the letters are held inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Lodge a protest inside a fortnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb meaning protest, but it is a noun: an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is an aim or purpose, so it is an object one pursues.

clue.text: Left as a result of ungenerous arrogance

parts.note: near is an old sense meaning mean or stingy
side means pretentious airs or swagger

explanation.surface: Someone departed because of mean-spirited haughtiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The NEARSIDE in Britain is the left side of a vehicle, nearer the kerb.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the nearside of a car is its left side, the side next to the kerb.

clue.text: Strong colour-not forgo ahead types

definitions.meaning: a vivid primary colour like blood
read as not for go-ahead types: a traffic light showing this means stop

explanation.walkthrough: 'forgo ahead' is a run-together 'for go-ahead': a stop light is no use to those who want to press on.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a bold primary colour, and a traffic signal of that hue means stop.

clue.text: Many note a role appears miscast

parts.note: G is a note of the musical scale

indicators.note: miscast suggests the letters have been cast in the wrong positions, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Many think an actor's part has been given to the wrong performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' means in abundance; GALORE follows its noun, as in 'prizes galore'.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore means in abundance, so it suggests a great many.

clue.text: A youngster with some spirit

definitions.meaning: a small measure of whisky or rum

explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small child and also a small dram of liquor.

clue.text: Centre-spread about Conservative minister's address

indicators.note: centre means we keep only the middle letters of the following word

parts.note: C abbreviates circa, Latin for about
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A newspaper's middle pages feature a Tory minister's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre-spread' suggests a magazine's middle pages; it means the middle of SPREAD. 'minister' is a clergyman, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectory is the house provided for a parish clergyman, his home.

clue.text: They always display the stars and stripes

definitions.text: They always display the stars and stripes

parts.words: They always display the stars and stripes
parts.note: not American patriots: military ranks are marked by stars on the shoulders and stripes on the sleeve

explanation.definitionFit: Military commanders wear insignia of rank such as stars and stripes.

clue.text: Sound man-he has cut down

definitions.meaning: a colloquial spelling that sounds like fellow, a man
one who fells trees, a lumberjack

explanation.definitionFit: Feller is a dialect form of fellow, and a feller is someone who chops down trees.

clue.text: Needs to be put straight over the right transmitter

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first part stands above the next
the letters are to be put in order, straightened out into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something has to be corrected regarding the proper radio equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sender is a device that transmits signals.

clue.text: Mediocre rider, that's made plain

indicators.note: the letters are made into something else, plainly rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter

explanation.surface: A poor horseman, which has been made obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-rate means of poor quality, inferior.

clue.text: Limits the area for stock

definitions.meaning: the bounds or scope within which something varies
open grazing land where cattle roam

explanation.definitionFit: A range is a scope between limits, and also open grazing land for cattle.

clue.text: Beautiful stuff as demonstrated

definitions.meaning: protested by occupying a place, staging a sit-in

explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a lustrous fabric, and protesters who sat in staged a demonstration.

clue.text: Convention demands an advisory board

definitions.meaning: a body of people that advises or governs

explanation.definitionFit: A council is a deliberative assembly, and also an advisory body.

clue.text: Cross through lines written by a rhymester

parts.note: per means by way of or through
verse is poetry, lines a rhymer writes

explanation.surface: Someone goes across a poet's lines of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb meaning to pass over, but it is an adjective, contrary.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse means awkwardly contrary, so cross or obstinate.

clue.text: He made his name as a physicist-and a politician before that

definitions.text: He made his name as a physicist

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A scientist made his reputation, and was an elected politician before that.
explanation.walkthrough: The French physicist Ampère gave his name to the unit of electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre-Marie Ampere was a French physicist whose surname became the unit of current.
